originalInput.context: Synthetic tour rehearsal. Compare ordered cue coverage against independent nearest-cue retrieval.

cues.text: Welcome visitors at the museum entrance and introduce the guided tour.
Describe the landscape painting and the artist who painted it.
Explain the bronze sculpture and its casting technique.
End the tour by directing visitors to the gift shop and exit.

records.text: Welcome to the museum! I will be your guide today.
We will not describe the landscape painting or discuss the artist today.
The statue was made by pouring molten bronze into a mold.
Our visit is over. You can leave through the souvenir store on your right.

warning: Rehearsal worksheet only, not proof that a cue was spoken correctly or understood. Supplied text is manually segmented: at most one fragment per cue and one cue per fragment. Neural semantic similarity is not entailment or confidence; negation and repeated wording can mislink. Exact dynamic programming maximizes sum(cosine-floor) with optional skips and strict increasing cue positions; it may omit a semantically valid fragment to preserve order. Independent nearest-cue baseline uses the same approved fragments and original scores; its duplicates/reversals are pair counts, not accuracy. Holds remain in the audit and can conceal missing evidence. No audio transcription, sending or execution.
